title: On the Localized Transition of Pipe Poiseuille Flow Part II: The Role of Tensile Energy Flux Vector
content: This is the second article on the mechanical mechanism of laminar turbulent transition in pipe Poiseuille ﬂow, which is one of the most important topics in turbulence research [1,2], as a representative of a large category of wall-bounded ﬂows [3]. Traditional ﬂuid mechanics stability research focuses on the eﬀects of diﬀerent disturbances and pays less attention to the mechanical properties of ﬂow structures [4]. In this paper, the tensile energy ﬂux, which is renamed from the viscous energy ﬂux vector [5], and its divergence are deduced and visualized in pipe Poiseuille ﬂow. The tensile energy ﬂux vector is both zero at wall and in the center, and at a critical position 0.707R, the divergence of tensile energy ﬂux vector is zero. Once the tensile force ﬂow reaches its critical value [4], the critical position 0.707R is just the local position where onset of turbulence occurs, consistent with some experimental results [6]. This predicted position has a zenith angle of 45° if membrane theory of spherical shell is applied on the ﬂuid [4], and this angle may be analogous to the cracks angle in the uniaxial compressive strength experiment of rock specimen subjected to uniaxial compression [7]. This article also proves that the critical Reynolds number during laminar turbulent transition in a circular tube is not a constant, but the ratio of critical tensile energy ﬂux to average kinetic energy ﬂux inside the tube is inversely proportional to the Reynolds number, similar to the inverse relationship between laminar ﬂow resistance coeﬃcient and Reynolds number.
